findings.title: Cleanup background job interval changed from 10 minutes to 1 minute
findings.body: `CleanUpService.Run` changes `time.NewTicker(time.Minute * 10)` to `time.NewTicker(time.Minute * 1)` without mention in the PR description. This appears to be a leftover from local testing and will cause all cleanup jobs (temp files, snapshots, dashboard versions, images, annotations, user invites, short URLs, query history) to run 10x more frequently in production, increasing database load. Note also that `clean` uses a 9-minute timeout (line 89), which was chosen to fit inside the original 10-minute tick interval.

findings.title: Debug logging left at Error level and logs full ID slice on every cleanup batch
findings.body: In `CleanAnnotations` (lines 534, 537, 554, 557) and `CleanOrphanedAnnotationTags` (lines 576, 579), `r.log.Error` is called unconditionally on every batch iteration even when there is no error (`err` is guaranteed `nil` at lines 534, 554, and 576), and it logs the entire `ids` slice (up to `AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize` elements). This looks like leftover debugging code and will flood error logs with large ID arrays during normal cleanup runs.

findings.title: Quadratic string concatenation when building SQLite DELETE statement for large batches
findings.body: In `deleteByIDs`, when running on SQLite with `AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize > 999`, the `IN` list is built in a loop with `values = fmt.Sprintf("%s, %d", values, v)` (lines 609-612). Because strings in Go are immutable, each iteration copies the entire accumulated string, resulting in O(N^2) allocations and time for N IDs (e.g., 32,767 IDs in the added test case). Use `strings.Builder` or `strconv.AppendInt` into a byte slice (as done in `getAccessControlFilter` at lines 387-395) instead.

findings.title: SQLite parameter limit check compares configured batch size instead of actual number of IDs
findings.body: Line 608 checks `r.cfg.AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize > sqliteParameterLimit`, and the `else` branch (line 615) binds `len(ids)` parameters (`?`). If `len(ids)` is small (for example, 1 or 2 rows on the final batch) while `AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize > 999`, it unnecessarily inlines literals; conversely, if `deleteByIDs` is ever called with `len(ids) > 999` when `AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize <= 999` (or unconfigured/0), it will exceed SQLite's parameter limit. Checking `len(ids) > sqliteParameterLimit` directly matches the actual number of bound parameters.
